pieces.title: If Walls Could Speak (eulogy, prose-poem)
pieces.text:
If walls could speak

I think they'd speak of your laughter first Not the loud kind, but your extremely high pitched laugh almost pricking our ears but never in an annoying way, it felt likr home, like something familiar and like something ours

If the walls could speak,

Our cafe hoppings would remind us your dark and hillarious jokes, your obsession for pictures with food, how when our order would arrive our inner critiques would come out. Our gossip sessions, deep talks, crazy photo sessions, fighting for each other's food Oh dear

They would rememeber us for our carefree, 0 civic sense, balling out laughter that would make our stomach hurt and suddenly our

world would feel lighter

Oh and the club walls would have crazy stories

They'd remember us as the craziest and messiest people.

They'd remember us so under influence, dancing terribly qnr perfectly at the same time- holding each other for support because we were apparently tooo drunk to even stand straight. Shouting lyrics at each other's faces like our life dependent on it. 2/5

They'd remember you crying one moment and laughing the other like nothing ever happened. How you used to take care of us no matter how drunk you were yourself, somehow always in your senses.

Superpower much

If the classroom walls could speak,

They'd laugh first

They'd talk about how impossible it was for us to stay serious during the whole class. Subway surfer on tabs, airpods blasting music, movie marathons, games, gossips, standing in punishments together almost everything except paying attention

And the quiet moments, those mattered the most.

The walks to home, telling each other how broke we were and the next moment food in our hands, giggling shamelessly throughout. Peeling food without being asked to, cooking for each other in times of illness, saving last bite, remembering preferences, tiny acts of devotion disguised as habits

That was your love language. You made people feel cared by your mundane acts that they almost went unnoticed

Almost.

If the walls could speak,

They wouldnt only talk about your death, they would also talk about your phrases, your accent, your patented words, stupid jokes, wierdass reactions. The way you cared for us got woven into our lives amd routines that parts of you still survives in us. And thats thr strangest thing 4/5

Even if right now you are not with us, yet every one of us still speaks a little like you, loves a little like you, takes care of people a little like you

As if you refuse to leave us and we love it

Rip baby

pieces.title: Nothing's wrong (monologue)
pieces.text:
Nothing's wrong,
I don't know
What's wrong
With me
At least…
nothing I can see.
And still
my chest feels heavy.
Not pain.
Not panic.
Just… weight.

I look for some reason.
A moment maybe.
Maybe a mistake.
Something to blame,
For my heart's flame.

But there's nothing.
Just silence.
No, noise...
Nothing,
And that's
What scares me!

because I can't find
what's wrong…
maybe
it's everything,
Or maybe
There's nothing
Wrong! But still
My chest ache
Like nothing normal.

pieces.title: What Is Love? (essay by Diya)
pieces.text:
To love is to let go, to love is to hold on, to love is to cherish people despite their flaws . The definitions for love are one too many to count. Yet when I say I love this person, somehow most of these definitions seem like half fits. So I often find myself asking this question What really is love? Is it when my father feeds me with his own hands when I don't want to eat?  or my mother saving the last piece of cake for me when she absolutely loves it more than me? Or perhaps it is when a friend remembers me whenever they see a cup of coffee. Or is it when my dog jumps to greet me the moment I am home. Yet all these are actions that show love but they aren't quite a definition so again what is love?
             As I sat with those definitions and actions and words I thought to myself and came up with my own conclusion. Now that perhaps maybe as flawed and incorrect as may be but here's my perspective on love quite unfiltered 
            Many people say I would die for the person I love but that is the first point I would disagree with. If I love someone then I would stay that means I would live for them so I could be by their side a bit longer to enjoy the warmth they radiate. To love someone is to cherish them despite their flaws. Absolutely but it is also to make them aware of their flaws and push them to be a better person. To love someone is to remember things they like,make food for them, going on walks with them. It is to spend time with them and make their lives easier along the way. To love is never just a word it is always to prove it through actions by putting them first. 
                  Now comes a tough debate , some say to love is to let go while others say to love is to hold on. Both of the definitions seem so contradictory yet both are right in their own perspectives So I thought about it and both of them seem incomplete. When I say to love someone is to let them go I mean I would let them go if it meant their happiness because forcing them to stay? That's not love that just means I am attached to them and I am not ready to let go of how they make me feel. So then To love is to hold on ? Well to love is to hold on even when things get tough. When there are 1000 reasons to leave finding that one reason to stay with them because staying with them makes it worth it. That I would say is love. 
                 So in the end you may ask me that Diya what is love ? and well to be honest I wouldn't have a definition ready for you. But I can tell you this much that love is felt by actions and it is a feeling so mixed filled with both joy and sorrow that perhaps it can't be defined and can only be felt regardless of similarities,differences,merits or flaws. It is something that has given people a purpose to live since the beginning of time

pieces.title: Why am I still alive? (war-survivor poem)
pieces.text:
Why am I still alive?
I should have been dead like others.
Does my time is yet to come,
Or maybe they want me to turn.

What was the mistake of my sleeping brother?
Was he holding guns or launching missile
Or was he conspire against the race to genocide.
Maybe because he was insect, they carry pesticide.

Why was my dad shot with breads in hand?
Was bread mock the presence of mighty neighbour
Or was my dad riding on tank with gun in hand.
Maybe because he was holding memory of his motherland.

Why I had to find my mom beneath the rubble?
Was she commanding an army to your land
Or was my home build on your Holy soil.
Maybe because letting her live was heavy toil.

Why did my sister was raped by cloaked man?
Was her appearance threaten your greater kingdom
Or was a toy to be raged upon by tying her dad.
Maybe because breaking bones isn't enough so you rage to break souls.

Why did a 6 month old infant had to die?
Was he mock, torture or plan to kill
Or was he just cleansing of land you need.
Maybe your blind dirty eyes can see what you bleed.

Why am I still alive?
Am I left behind just to see.
Does my time is yet to come maybe,
left to suffer on memories of people gone.

Why did I have to see this Eid?
All the echoes run from autumn back to spring,
I am scared and worried, can't think but fear.
Thoughts running with tears in back to see whom to lose this year.

pieces.title: Ghost (confessional poem)
pieces.text:
When i was a kid i used to fear ghosts 
Ghost who would come at night 
Hide under my bed, 
Behind the curtains
Or beneath every dark corner of my room.

I surpassed adulthood,seen life for 21 years.

I still fear ghost 
But A different ghost,

A Ghost who would also come at night
In disguise of realisation and guilt
Hide behind my eyes
Behind the skin
Or Beneath my chest.

Kid me had a mom to run to 
when fear befalls 
Had torch to chase away 
The darkness had a warm lap 
To sleep on while being trembled

But adult me?

What about him?
A lonely sculpture,with no heart
With a hollow chest filled with regrets
Where would he run to?

How would he chase away the ghost 
from his head? 
Who would he run to seek shelter 
from the dark clouds?

I think there is a ghost residing 
beneath my skull
Waiting for the darkness to come
So that he can torment me 
for all the deeds I did
So that he can rip my chest off
Pull my heart out
Peel the skin
Tear every vein of it
Crush it untill the flesh turns 
into a stack of rot cell

The ghost finally won,
I just died last night
The reckoning of all my deeds 
have completed

I was alloted hell again
The same hell I feard all my life
And The Ghost won the bettle
The battle between pain, fear and life
Won when life just gives up....

pieces.title: Unsent love letter (v2, AABB)
pieces.text:
I love looking at beautiful thing,
And you must imagine flower or spring.
But no darling beautiful is only your face,
But I as nobody always dare to take it's grace.

One day you might just be mine,
That day, the only time my life will shine.
Let's not rush to deliver a proposal speech,
(Cause)
I know that you might be here just to teach.

Do I have eyes which can see?
(Cause)
Your beauty must be paid, not free!
Now I wonder what will me without you,
Maybe life will be just sad without any clue.

Atlast let's consider what if you choose him,
That would be nice because he is good and slim.
Is he athe favourite of almighty God?
Or am I entangled in fate's dark odd!

He stands in the darkness, waiting for his turn,
To warm up his hands on the fire which I burn.
He sits beside the embers I bled out to explode.
And borrows our warmth just to claim he is your light.

He appears like a canvas that’s easy to love,
While I’m just a mess you’re scared to speak of.
(Maybe)
He seek for the moment I slip or might fall,
To rush in and offer to provide you it all.

Still, a tiny bit hope keeps on pulling my chest,
That maybe someday you will prefer me as best.
That you’ll smile at scars and cry at mess, I hold.
And maybe choose my warm chaos to all of his gold.

I’m scripting this letter knowing I’ll never able to send,
Perhaps to experience the heartbreak before it can end.
I’d rather be cozy to bleed out on this quiet blank page,
Than letting you see me falling down on your stage.

One day these pages may also turn yellow and old,
Their edges torn, their stories dry, crumbling cold.
But every faded line of history shall also prove 
That the bravest letters are the ones that never move.

(But still)
If he’s your final call, I’ll just smile and step back,
And probably paint over all leftover invisible crack.
I’ll weep that he provide you the world that you crave,
While I stand as a lonely servant inside my own grave.

pieces.title: The Great Separation (ABABCC pastiche)
pieces.text:
We past by the reverend walls where once we wear the gown,    No desire to wander at random through the lime-walk's shade;    Loud thunder music dies within the college town, Where eternal hours of youth and intellect were made.  The racing paddles are still, the festive halls grew cold,    And that cast thin drifts, before our hearts grew old. 
Then arrives the Great Separation,fierceful and stark, To turn our passing freedom into a focused toil; We then bend our captive knee to facts lying in dark,    And hold our red noses to the grindstone's soil.    Like a melancholy madness shaking all heavy heads,    We trade our gleaming dreams for dull and routine beds.   
We try to summon the remembrance of things past, But have no power left to climb upon that floor; Another name is revealed where our hopes were once cast,    And keyless shadow locks have barred the ancient door. We try to mask our weariness, pretending all is quite well, While slow and secret poison cast its quiet spell.
It starts as some ignored ache, a dull, sickly strain,    A light and passing migraine arrive in the morning dew;    A tiny separable spite that nests within our brain, And galls the soft buds of all the friends we ever knew.    We cover ourselves in weeds of work to ease the smart,  Ignoring to know the cold disease is creeping to the heart.
The silent illness evolve, a hard and hidden mass, An inward developing tumor mining deep within;  And feeds upon our souls while busy seasons pass, And record the ulcerous places of our darkest sin. No soap can cleanse this foul darkness, a systemic rot,    That consumes the sweetest memories we have forgot.   
And at last, the cancer spreads, a human ending force, Some call it guilt, the final harvest of eternal shame;    We are twain forever, bound to this distant falling course, And cannot find the courage to breathe each other’s name.    The deep, hard and cold vase of chilling tears is now frozen dry,   And under this inky blots, our dead expectations shall lie.

pieces.title: Love Letter to Kashi
pieces.text:
I espied the ghats as I held your hands in mine,
When I touched you at Assi, faith began to shine,
Ganga stood serene, she did not flow, she just watched,
How my fingers cradled yours as they held thee,
From Assi to Manikarnika's eternal sacred holy fire,
Every step I took with you as I held you higher.
At Dashashwamedh, the bright lamps for prayer began to rise,
I folded my hands as I wrapped them around yours, so wise,
We leaned on each other's shoulders and witnessed the sacred Ganga Aarti divine,
Both conch and bells rang high into the peaceful night,
Your soft palm in mine became my diya's light,
We floated a diya in Ganga's stream,
I held your hand tightly and prayed for my dream.
Benaras held us closer and never let these memories part,
Its beautiful lanes were made just for hand-in-hand and heart-to-heart,
Malaiyo, incense, chai, Banarasi saree and kulhad chai,
We lost our way as we held hand-in-hand all day,
You softly told me that we should not go and should just stay,
I held you tighter and let Kashi make our forever way.
Barefoot to Shree Kashi Vishwanath Dham, I held your hands tightly,
The gold-spire glowed, but you were my strength, my heart, my light,
Innumerable devotees with folded hands prayed for silver and gold,
I held your hand firmly because you were my last and forever gift,
Forehead on marble, you locked your fingers in mine,
I prayed that Mahadev would let you be only mine in the next birth too.
All said Kashi freed us from birth and pain,
But as I held your hand, I wanted to be born again,
At Manikarnika where fire burned, flowers bloomed nearby,
You kissed my forehead and said you would always stay by my side,
Life and death met there under the same clear sky,
Ganga cleansed every sin except love because it was so sacred,
And there I learned that moksha was nothing but holding you tightly.
So, my love, I wanted to explore everything with you,
Be my man, be my gali, be my ghat and be my prayer,
Be my aarti, be my Kashi, be my love language and be my breath of air,
When the last diya faded and bells became still,
When the moon silently faded over Ganga's holy water,
I still stood there and held your hand in mine,
I forever wrote your name in Ganga every year,
For every birth we saw,
My only prayer was that you and your hand stayed forever in me.

pieces.title: Soul of Dead Ink
pieces.text:
Title:Soul of dead ink

I am a mountain now without rock,
Infact I'm the lost sheep of my own flock.
Let me take you to a fine golden hour,
An hour feels year ago when I opt for an flower.
A time until which all I felt like a imposter.
Then the almighty sun arrives to make mah life a roller coaster.

"I know the feeling that it's just another poetry,
But believe me she change my life into part of history."

I don't know, how to rhyme or sing,
But at that time I was in love, open to fling.
All I knew is that thy servent wasn't worthy of angels love.
My stonesaffectionated with thy pearls, desire to strike thy glove.
The black raven called turmoil is my name,
Or maybe I'm just nobody with no fame.

"You must be thinking this poem has not structure.
But when I describe her my entire body and soul got puncture."

The days passed in seconds while I watch her pass by,
The drops of Olympus fell, I grasp the sign to chase her as I fly.
She felt like intimacy of my all beloved so far.
This timeless moment is definition of serenity not a scar.
Echo of heart beat was not present, the doubt arrive in my heart.
The panic begins with just a thought of burden to fulfill desire of this art.

"But then this strike that why does this world stop revolving around me,
Then I noticed that my soul has already departure that my body has paid the fee."

Slowly the echoes of living fade away,
Alas my dying soul still wanted to see her ray.
At that moment all I desire to touch her last time,
But sadly the body was past turn worthless like a dime.
An angel asked my weeping soul, didn't she left you before,
I replied, Sun did brought draught to my land, but just look at her and adore.

"Angel smiled saying you are in heaven look at the beauty here.
The tears in my face replied her all about my Sun's bright flare."

Now maybe the almighty has blessed me with heaven,
All I do is curse my fate as just wanted to spend a min or seven.
I was once asked "Did thy heart die to see her loved by another"
I replied, "My friend I die because I saw her in all her beauty."
He continued, "What devil's tongue is this?"
I looked beneath, "I am like a eye and she is Sun, couldn't able to take it long."

"He replied you lost the track of rhyming....
I replied because it's life not everything is poetic."

Thus my life ended as I couldn't take the beauty,
Maybe I fullfill my role to love, which was my duty.
I guess that's why the almighty have send me here to rest.
But you know (readers) it's not fair as she is all I have in my chest.
All I can pray for her life and happiness....
And Hope so her good life will reduce my emptiness....

"Sorry to disappoint but it's not a poetry
And in my life sad that I didn't win the lottery"

And if not for her existence then,

I am a mountain just without rock.
You can say I'm an ocean without water.
Maybe desert without any sand.
Or perhaps forrest without a single tree.
A sky without freedom and Hope.
Maybe she existing with him is my sisypus's rock.

pieces.title: Jantar Mantar protest poem ("I wish I didn't belong")
pieces.text:
the poem below regarding jantar mantar students protest  


  I wish I didn't belong to this age,
Where to seek knowledge, 
One has to pass through Humans rage.

I just wish I didn't belong among this race
When marching for rights,
Will be necessary for educational pace.

I wish I'd suffer from stroke,
Better than to see students bones
Being toyed and rights being a joke.

I wish I wouldn't be part of this mankind,
Where marching women being harrassed 
By protector who are totally blind.

I wish I could just shut off my eyes,
Where students seeking for knowledge 
Will be treated as vicious spies.

I wish I never have an open heart,
Thus the evil nature of all ruling god
Could fool me to think him as smart.

I wish I never be behind the distance bar,
Where pursuit of better future,
Will give you token of heavy scar.

I wish We never be on side of losing,
Where to exercise your right,
Will make you regret of your choosing.

I wish we could change yesterday,
Where they act as god
And played with us like we are of clay.

I wish I could speak of better tomorrow,
But the act within nation's vicinity 
Is only bringing tears and heart full of sorrow.
